findings.reason: §6's central "three changes" narrative must be rewritten to name the landed node and point the remaining work at jtmm-angle-factor-retire alone, or §6 re-authorises work already done.
findings.text: §6 states "the engine gains a pol_angle_like branch that applies no COCOS-digit factor and takes the angle's rotation sense only from the binding's authored sign_convention, refusing a binding whose sense is unknown-unvalidated"; that branch already exists (_poloidal_angle_sense_factor at imas_ambix/data/transform_engine.py:425, dispatched at :456), it was already landed by commit b72dcfab and is guarded by tests/data/test_transform_engine.py:751,780, so an implementer reading §6 as a spec would rebuild a guard the tree already carries

findings.reason: the §6 prior-art sentence is now false and would send a worker to add a supplier that is present.
findings.text: §6 states "read_geometry_table applies nothing for probe_angle_source description today, so that branch fills each probe's angle from the emitted poloidal_angle"; that branch already exists (description_reader.py:253-255, `_supply_declared_probe_angles` at :55, `_PROBE_ANGLE_DD_PATH` at :85), landed by the same b72dcfab and hardened by jtmm-probe-angle-guards

findings.reason: the §6 interface account ("ambix retires one public definition") counts a retirement already made, under-counting net surface change.
findings.text: §6 states "mast_angle_to_canonical has no production caller (its only caller is its own test in tests/test_cocos.py, which retires with it), ... so §6 retires it"; the symbol is already absent from the tree — imas_ambix/cocos.py __all__ (lines 111-120) no longer exports it, and b72dcfab removed both the function and its test reference — so §6's retirement clause names a symbol that no longer exists

findings.reason: §6 lists as new a definition the plan already shipped; the prose must record the landing so no node re-creates it.
findings.text: §6 states "The generic entry is one new public definition ... measure_convention(records, eligibility, *, shots)"; that exact function already exists at convention.py:283, is already exported (__all__ line 353), and measure_diiid_convention already delegates to it with DIIID_ELIGIBILITY (line 333-341), landed by jtmm-convention-entry (cd8e9a7a, review 112/120)

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — every new behaviour lands behind an existing deep module (eddb.py, transform_engine.py, cocos_convention.py, description_reader.py, eval/efit_referee.py) whose interface is unchanged; no section spreads one mechanism across parallel wrappers.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: pass — each shared mechanism is extended at its owner (eddb.py write_channel helpers shared by the grid writer; machine_identity.default_registry keyed per machine; the probe angle supplied by read_geometry_table's own selector branch), and the plan names each owner it extends.
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — public_definitions 0, cli_options 0, mcp_views 0, refusal_families 0; every section that adds a public definition carries an interface account in its own text (§2 exporter "retires nothing, because ambix has no exporter"; §6 "one definition retired and one added"; §7 "retires three public definitions and their re-export, and adds one, the table").
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — §6's implementation narrative describes as future work the pol_angle_like engine branch, the description probe-angle supplier and the retirement of cocos.mast_angle_to_canonical, all three of which are already in the tree (b72dcfab), and it states that measure_convention and the generic convention kernel are still to be written when they exist (cd8e9a7a).
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — the readers the plan adds are justified replacements, not wrappers: read_signal_map_observation replaces the consumerless read_catalogue_observation, and the FAME/SELENE equilibrium maps extend the signal-map owner rather than layering over it.
